purpose: The 5 hand-crafted observation states for the prompt-only baseline gate in plan.md Section 7 (Phase 0 -> Phase 1 checklist, item 7). Pass condition per case: (a) mentions every object present in the state, (b) mentions no object absent from it, (c) reads as a single dated entry rather than a list of facts. 4/5 passing -> proceed. <=1/5 -> the prompt needs work before any fine-tuning discussion.
construction: Each state was hand-written from a real ORACC diary entry drawn from the 807 zero-gap usable units. The reference_text is the actual historical entry and is NEVER shown to the model - it exists so a human can compare register afterwards. Cases deliberately span five different phenomenon types so the test is not five variations of one conjunction.
leakage_note: The three few-shot examples in scripts/baseline_prompt.py are different diary entries from these five. They share phenomenon types (that is the point of few-shot) but no case text appears in the prompt.

cases.reference_text: Night of the 11th, beginning of the night, the moon was 1 cubit 8 fingers in front of δ Capricorni.
cases.observation_state:
<TRADITION=BABYLONIAN>
<GENRE=OBSERVATION>
<OBSERVATION_STATE>
  Date: year 49 of the Seleucid Era, month V, night of the 11th
  Watch: beginning of the night
  Moon: visible, waxing, confidence: high
  Events: [{"event":"conjunction","objects":["Moon","delta Capricorni"],"relation":"in front of","separation":"1 cubit 8 fingers","confidence":"high"}]
</OBSERVATION_STATE>
<ENTRY>

  Events: [{"event":"first_appearance","objects":["Venus"],"direction":"east","sign":"Scorpius","rising_to_sunrise_deg":10,"ideal_first_appearance":"the 11th","confidence":"medium"}]

cases.phenomenon: first lunar visibility of the month with a lunar-six interval
cases.reference_text: Month IX, the 1st (of which followed the 30th of the preceding month), sunset to moonset: 17°; it was bright; earthshine; it was low to the sun.
cases.observation_state:
<TRADITION=BABYLONIAN>
<GENRE=OBSERVATION>
<OBSERVATION_STATE>
  Date: year 45 of the Seleucid Era, month IX, the 1st
  Month start: the 1st followed the 30th of the preceding month
  Moon: first visibility, brightness: bright, earthshine: present, low to the sun, confidence: high
  Events: [{"event":"lunar_first_visibility","objects":["Moon"],"sunset_to_moonset_deg":17,"confidence":"high"}]
</OBSERVATION_STATE>
<ENTRY>
cases.allowed_extra_note: the Sun is implicit in 'sunset to moonset' and 'low to the sun', so mentioning it is not a hallucinated object here

criterion_e_note: required_facts added after the template control exposed that criterion (a) checks only object NAMES. The template scored 5/5 while silently dropping the watch, the latitude clause, the month number, earthshine and the direction - all of them hard facts present in the OBSERVATION_STATE. Criterion (e) checks that the quantitative and qualitative facts survive, which is what the guardrail in plan.md Section 2 actually promises. Each fact is a list of acceptable surface variants; it counts as present if any variant appears.
criterion_f_note: required_relation added after qwen2.5:7b produced 'Venus and Mars were 3 fingers below, with Venus 2 fingers back to the west' for a state whose fact is 'Venus below Mars'. Every token criterion (e) looks for was present, so it passed, while the conjunction relationship itself had been destroyed - the reader cannot tell which body was below which. plan.md Section 2 names exactly this ('a reversed relationship') as the thing a regex/NER validator cannot catch. Criterion (f) checks that OBJ1, the relation word, and OBJ2 appear in that ORDER, which catches reversal and destruction of the pairing. It does not make the whitelist sufficient - the hand-built 30-50 case adversarial set in plan.md Section 2 is still the primary evidence.
